page: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. It is equipped with 21.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 2.62 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not included, meaning storage relies entirely on external network-attached volumes.

The instance is network and EBS optimized, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory operations. The Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the middle 50% tier, as do the Passmark CPU and memory scores. The processor supports AVX and AVX-512f instruction sets, which assist in vector calculations, though its performance in the Passmark CPU physics test and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

In terms of memory bandwidth, the instance achieves average results for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. However, it exhibits limitations in large language model inference, with prompt processing on a 7B model rated as poor and text generation on the same model rated as weak. This hardware profile is suited for network-bound compute workloads, static web serving, and database operations that do not require local NVMe storage or high-density memory configurations.
